      "observations": [
        "The complete one-path human diff adds a handler-local numeric counter initialized to 0 and a yield after every 25 response or sync-response branches. The fixed accepted code retains both. The counter sits after deletion, unchanged-ETag, fetch-queue, pagination and error/ignore branches; it does not count only successfully synchronized calendar items.",
        "The counter increments after response handling, awaits a timer when it reaches 25, then resets before the method clears tag and appends closing XML. The existing awaited tree walk suspends at endElement and reaches endDocument afterward. This preserves local parsing order; it does not turn doWebDAVSync into a promise for every later multiget or provider callback.",
        "Current getUpdatedItems creates a new WebDAV handler when the server advertises support. endDocument retains the separate batch, changed-item multiget, token/page and finalization decisions. Existing focused yield-boundary knowledge is reused; no multiget threshold or global batch-size policy is inferred.",
        "No tests change. The bounded existing test_caldav_sync directly checks non-ASCII text in logXML after its mock request and executeSoon; it has no counter, timer, responsiveness or 25-response assertion. Its actual assertion message is nonempty and contains should.",
        "The new reason comment explains the responsiveness constraint and the yield is separated from the preceding response branches. The numeric shouldYieldEventLoop field uses a Boolean-looking name, but this is accepted local naming rather than a demonstrated defect or a global naming rule.",

Existing-account discovery uses the incoming mail server hostname; the account-hub branch normalizes the entered server URL and uses its hostname. Those are distinct inputs, not interchangeable endpoints.",

The replacement probes only configured hostname/activity metadata. No authentication, consent, token reuse or server-authorization result follows from a truthy provider object.",
        "The unchanged existing-account comment says CardDAV scope was not granted. Neither the historical two-argument provider implementation nor the fixed provider checks a stored user grant here. A concrete clarification would say the configured provider does not support CardDAV; the useful metadata-versus-grant distinction is captured in one focused source-supported lesson.",

Current hostname casing, newest-login sorting and passwordFromStore state are later accepted details, not changes credited to this patch.",

This later receiver contract does not prove a regression in the original built-in two-argument port, and a positive username-restricted extension-provider UI path remains a bounded gap.",
